needs: bytes in, bytes out (&[byte] to buffer.Buffer)
buffer.Buffer built with push in a loop (ownership moves round)
Result with a static message, buffer dropped on no path that returns Err
integer bit arithmetic by / and % (no shifts needed)
alphabet mapping both ways without a string table (byte arithmetic on ranges)
remainder handling of the last 1 or 2 bytes
strict validation before or while decoding
pitfalls: padding left off (length 2 or 3 mod 4) accepted
whitespace/newlines skipped (the lenient habit of most decoders)
non-zero trailing bits accepted (Python's own b64decode(validate=True) accepts them)
'=' accepted in the middle, or three '=', or 'A=AA'
'==' with a non-'=' after it, or a pad where the last group has 3 data chars and 2 pads
bytes of 128 or more in the text (int_of gives 128..255, negative-looking bugs if a signed compare is assumed)
encode: forgetting the padding, or using the wrong low bits for the last character
decode Err path leaking a half-built Buffer
reading text[i+3] past the end when length is not a multiple of 4
int_of(byte) values 128-255 in the data when encoding (a / 4 on a wrong sign would corrupt)
difficulty_notes: L2: two functions, no data structure, but strictness is a list of separate rules that a model tends to apply from the lenient decoder it knows (skip whitespace, optional padding, url-safe). 115 of the 329 oracle cases probe the trailing-bits rule, 43 length, 21 alphabet, 21 padding; the expected answers were cross-checked between Python base64, an independent regex built from the RFC, and hand-typed RFC 4648 section 10 vectors. Oracle also runs lengths 0..8 and every possible penultimate character before '==' and '='.
